The independently admitted localization runtime supplies the exact positional compatibility contract needed by platform.ts.
An explicit one-time Proctor resource-root interface replaces the ambient VS Code product global without weakening FileAccess behavior.
The experimental reducer is outside the approved static closure and is not exported by the admitted observable facade; its dedicated cases are removed as one explicit behavior exclusion.
This experimental time facade is outside the approved static closure; the non-experimental throttledObservable implementation and its owner suite are retained.

The suite is coupled to errorMessage.ts outside the approved closure; admitted error routing, cancellation, and serialization dependencies remain exercised by assert, async, event, lifecycle, and observable owner suites.
It owns marshalling.ts, which is outside the approved closure; marshallingIds.ts is a constants-only dependency and no reduced marshalling substitute is introduced.

dependencies.rationale: The independently admitted compatibility seam satisfies platform localization without VS Code bootstrap or language-pack globals.
Process composition configures the application resource root explicitly instead of relying on an ambient VS Code product global.
The pinned Node and Electron Chromium runtimes provide the standard interfaces declared by the complete common closure.
A local adapter preserves the Mocha-style callback and skip semantics used by upstream assertions without admitting Mocha or Sinon.
The pinned compiler executes upstream TypeScript namespaces and parameter properties with the admitted useDefineForClassFields semantics.

divergences.summary: VS Code localization and product-resource globals are replaced by explicit Proctor-owned one-time configuration seams; positional NLS and FileAccess behavior remain verified.

Mocha globals and Sinon stubs are adapted to a Node 24 runner, a small callback/skip adapter, and a local callable stub while retaining upstream assertions, ordering, fake time, platform skips, and failure behavior.

The experimental reducer and time facade are not part of the approved static runtime closure; the reducer-only section of the observable suite is the sole removed owner-test section, while non-experimental throttling and debug suites are retained.

Dedicated production and test compiler profiles retain upstream class-field, namespace, decorator, DOM, unchecked-index, and import semantics instead of mechanically rewriting the admitted source to the generic Proctor profile.

Leak tracking and observable debug/RPC mechanics remain in source and owner tests, but no Proctor preload or renderer capability exposes them; production entrypoints select only explicit imports and esbuild tree-shakes unused debug exports.

Type-only import annotations preserve upstream compiler elision while making the runtime dependency graph explicit. These source edits (and the transaction module's trailing whitespace cleanup) are adaptations rather than undeclared copy transformations.

The source DOM stylesheet bridge uses CSP-compatible StyleSheetHandle change/removal events; each cloned sheet is owned and disposed with its source/target window. No inline-style or HTML sink fallback is introduced.

verification.obligation: Compile and execute every transferred owner suite under Node 24, preserving async timing, ordering, cancellation, disposal, leak diagnostics, resources, URI behavior, observables, virtual scheduling, and upstream skips.

Type-check the transferred suites and support without weakening the production compiler profile.
Bundle and execute localization, DisposableStore, and Emitter in the pinned sandboxed Electron Chromium renderer and verify the interactive event path.

Verify declaration-only dependencies remain analyzable while every executable source cycle is rejected.
Verify schema, every local digest and marker, license reference, unique ownership, divergence, and evidence parity without a VS Code checkout.
